hypotheses.statement: For every fixed real $\alpha$ with $1\leq\alpha<2$, approximating Vertex Cover within factor $\alpha$ is NP-hard. Thus, unless $\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}$, no deterministic polynomial-time algorithm achieves factor $2-\varepsilon$ for any fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$.

For every fixed rational $\sigma\in(0,1)$, there are nonempty constant alphabets and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from $\mathrm{3SAT}$ to instances of the form above such that satisfiable formulas give $\mathop{\mathrm{val}}(\Phi)=1$, and unsatisfiable formulas give $\mathop{\mathrm{val}}(\Phi)\leq\sigma$.

The family $\mathcal I$ is hereditary and contains every coordinate singleton. Formula [graph:norm-definition] defines a norm. For each fixed query $i$, the increment is linear in $s$ and obeys $$\label{graph:increment} \left\|z(i,s)\right\|_*\leq\|s\|_\infty.$$

For a fixed integer $m\geq4$, a fixed even square $d$ satisfying [src:dimension-bounds](#src:dimension-bounds), and fixed source alphabets, the graph $G$ can be output explicitly in deterministic time polynomial in the source bit length. Every edge test is exact.

If $T_1,\ldots,T_d$ are independent uniform elements of $\mathcal T$, then $$\label{graph:tail}
 \Pr\left[\sum_{j=1}^dT_j>t\right]
 >\frac12-\sqrt2\left(a+\frac1{\sqrt d}\right)
 >\frac12-\frac1m.$$
If $\mathop{\mathrm{val}}(\Phi)=1$, then $G$ has an independent set of size greater than $(1/2-1/m)n$. Consequently, $$\tau(G)<\left(\frac12+\frac1m\right)n.$$

Suppose an independent set contains at least $b_0n$ vertices with $\left\|S_v\right\|_*>t$. There is a fixed nonempty finite set $A_*\subset\mathbb R^{\mathcal P}$ such that $$\Pr_{v\in V(G)}[S_v\in A_*]\geq b_0,
 \qquad
 \left\|x+y\right\|_*>2t\quad(x,y\in A_*),$$ where the vertex is uniform. For a nonempty finite set $B$, write $\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_*(z,B)=\min_{b\in B}\left\|z-b\right\|_*$. The function $$F(z)=\frac12\bigl(\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_*(z,-A_*)-\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_*(z,A_*)\bigr)
 \label{ana:distance-function}$$ is odd and $1$-Lipschitz for $\left\|\cdot\right\|_*$, and $F(z)>t$ on $A_*$.*


*Let $\mathcal E=\binom{[d]}2$. Draw independent uniform occurrence seeds $\boldsymbol c=(c_e)_{e\in\mathcal E}\in[M]^{\mathcal E}$ and independent weight blocks $s_j$ uniform on $[-1,1]^r$, independently of the seeds. Put $$f(\boldsymbol c,\boldsymbol s)
    =F\left(\sum_{j=1}^d z(i_j(\boldsymbol c),s_j)\right).
 \label{ana:f}$$ This bounded function satisfies $$\mathbb E_{\boldsymbol s}f(\boldsymbol c,\boldsymbol s)=0
       \quad\hbox{for every }\boldsymbol c,
 \qquad
 \mathbb Ef^2\geq\nu d.
 \label{ana:variance}$$ On the weight cubes it has the following three oscillation bounds:*

1.  *Replacing one weight block $s_j$, with all other data fixed, changes $f$ by at most $2$.*

2.  *Replacing one seed $c_e$, with all other data fixed, changes $f$ by at most $4$.*

3.  *Fix $k\in[d]$. Simultaneously replacing any seeds incident to $k$, while keeping all nonincident seeds, all weights, and the question received at every opposite position $j\ne k$ from $\{j,k\}$ unchanged, changes $f$ by at most $2$.*

*The set $A_*$, the function $F$, and its formula are fixed from an independent set of the entire graph before the fresh seeds above are drawn. A seed enters $f$ only through its endpoint questions.

Let $\nu>0$ and let $h$ be an integer with $2\leq h\leq d$. Suppose the bounded Borel measurable function $f$ on $\Omega$ satisfies $$\label{res:variance-hypotheses} \mathbb E_{\mathbf s}f(\mathbf c,\mathbf s)=0 \quad\text{for every }\mathbf c, \qquad \mathbb Ef^2\geq\nu d.$$ Suppose also that the following oscillation bounds hold with all coordinates not mentioned kept fixed:* 1. *Changing one weight block $s_j$ changes $f$ by at most $2$.* 2. *Changing one seed $c_e$ changes $f$ by at most $4$.* 3. *For any $k\in[d]$, simultaneously changing seeds incident to $k$, while preserving $Q_{\{k,j\},j}(c_{\{k,j\}})$ for every $j\ne k$, changes $f$ by at most $2$.* *If $$\label{res:scale} 16h+32h^2\leq\frac{\nu d}{2},$$ then there are a fixed $h$-element set $J$ and fixed frozen data $\mathbf a$ such that $$\label{res:variance} \sum_{j\in J}\mathbb E_{u_j}\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}_{s_j}H_j(u_j,s_j) \geq\frac{\nu h}{4}.$$ The law in [res:variance] is the product law of the remaining hidden seeds and batch weights described above. In particular it is not conditioned on an event involving a draw of those remaining variables.

There is a deterministic measurable rule $g=(g_j)_{j\in J}\in\mathbb R^{J\times[r]}$, defined at every batch query and real-weight tuple, that equals $\nabla\psi_{\boldsymbol i}$ outside a finite union of proper affine hyperplanes for each fixed query tuple and fixed frozen data. At every tuple, $$g\in\mathop{\mathrm{conv}}\{\pm v_I(\boldsymbol i):I\in\mathcal I\}.
 \label{ana:hull}$$ Consequently, $$\|g_j\|_1\leq1,
 \qquad
 g_{j,t'}=0\quad\hbox{if }t'\notin
                   \operatorname{slot}_{i_j}(\Lambda_{i_j}).
 \label{ana:block-bound}$$ The rule uses the fixed formula for $F$, the frozen increments, and the supplied batch queries and weights. It does not inspect which hidden seed occurrences produced those queries.

For each $j\in J$ and supported own tuple $u$, the function $H_j(u,\cdot)$ is $1$-Lipschitz with respect to $\|\cdot\|_\infty$. For almost every own $s\in[-1,1]^r$, $$\partial_{s^{(t')}}H_j(u,s)=\bar g_{j,t'}(u,s),
 \qquad t'\in[r].
 \label{ana:conditional-derivative}$$ Its variance satisfies the dimension-independent bound $$\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}_s H_j(u,s)
       \leq2\mathbb E_s\|\bar g_j(u,s)\|_2^2.
 \label{ana:cube-variance}$$ Consequently, under the fixed restricted law, $$\sum_{j\in J}\mathbb E\|\bar g_j(u_j,s_j)\|_2^2
      \geq\nu h/8=\beta h.
 \label{ana:energy}$$

The functions $\mathcal L_j$ are deterministic total measurable maps returning at most $\ell$ valid labels. Once $\Phi,F,J,\boldsymbol a$ and the conditional kernels above are fixed, each list uses only its own questions $u_j$ and weights $s_j$. In particular it has no additional access to the actual hidden seed occurrences or to any other actual batch input. Under the fixed restricted product law, $$\mathbb EZ\geq\frac{\beta h}{2}=2.
 \label{ana:list-hits}$$

For every fixed $J,\mathbf a$ and fixed list maps satisfying [dec:local_lists](#dec:local_lists), $$\Pr(E_{jk})\leq\ell^2\sigma
 \quad(j,k\in J,\ j<k),
 \qquad
 \mathbb EZ\leq1+\binom h2\ell^2\sigma
       =\frac32-\frac1{2h}<\frac32.
 \label{dec:pair_bound}$$

For the graph constructed in [graph:section](#graph:section), assume [src:restriction-budget]. If $\mathop{\mathrm{val}}(\Phi)\leq\sigma$, every independent set has size strictly less than $n/m$. Consequently $\tau(G)>(1-1/m)n$.

coverage.checked_domain: Binary alphabets: every total binary projection and every four-entry weight tuple in {-1/2,0,1/2}, with two singleton scopes; additional empty, inconsistent, overlapping, and empty-scope boundary instances.
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent global binary assignment enumeration over every subset of blocks; exact Python Fraction arithmetic, compared with FLINT rational local-label enumeration.
